Union Minister Amit Shah during the 60th Raising Day event of Chandigarh Police. Photo: Youtube/@AmitShah
Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Sunday (November 1, 2026) said the Union government has resolved to build a drug-free India and Chandigarh will be the first city to be rid of drugs.
Also Read : Amit Shah visits Punjab; drug menace at centre stage yet again
“Now that we have resolved to build a drug-free India, Chandigarh will be the first city in the country to become drug-free. Following the implementation of the new criminal laws, Chandigarh Police has increased the conviction rate in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) related cases, securing the conviction of 93% of accused persons and sending them to jail,” he said.
“From August 4, 2024, till date, 8,206 FIRs have been registered in Chandigarh, of which Chandigarh Police has filed charge sheets online in 7,590 cases. The police have also ensured convictions in 85% of cases by improving the conviction rate,” Mr. Shah added.
The Minister was speaking during the Diamond Jubilee celebrations marking the establishment of Chandigarh Police and the President’s Colour Award Ceremony of Chandigarh Police.
Mr. Shah said policing in the country has largely remained focused on tackling terrorism, drugs, cybercrime, and maintaining law and order. However, providing ease of access to services for citizens is an important responsibility of the police, and through its beat policing app, Chandigarh Police has successfully implemented an “excellent system on the ground, ensuring that citizens do not have to visit police stations for their needs”, he said.
He said that the President’s Colour awarded to Chandigarh Police is a recognition of the force’s six decades of service, dedication and sensitivity.
